summary: The agent spent about 1.5 of its 8 allotted hours diagnosing and rewriting /app/dispatch.py and /app/planner/, independently finding essentially the full list of planted bugs described in the official solution (gross/net gas calorific value inversion, engine heat having nowhere to dump, ignoring start/stop costs and midnight state, UTC weather/tariff timestamp errors, incomplete part-load tables, intercooler heat miscounted, grid kVA ignoring generator reactive power, tower load missing compressor/AC1 power, missing B2 outage, PV inverter cap). It built its own independent reference model and ~60 synthetic test days to validate optimality before finishing. The verifier's hidden-day suite passed 53/55 checks (all balance, limit, availability, gas/cost-reporting and repeatability tests on all 5 days), but test_least_cost failed on two hidden days (h2 by ~0.17% over the optimum, h3 by ~23% over). The agent explicitly acknowledged in its final report that it used a conservative heuristic for when to hold absorption-chiller cooling water at 22°C (enabling it only when otherwise infeasible) rather than comparing the enable/disable branches every half-hour as the true optimum requires, and flagged this as an open design decision rather than a bug — this is exactly the author's stated core difficulty, and it produced the large h3 deviation (h3 is a spring/shoulder-season day, matching the agent's own prediction that this shortcut would cost 5-30% in shoulder seasons). The verifier reward is binary at 0 because not all tests passed, despite the overall solution being very close to correct.

task_specification.explanation: instruction.md directs the agent to derive all physical/operational rules from plant.json, supply.json, status.json and the engineers' narrative rather than spelling out exact modelling formulas, and the agent successfully reverse-engineered nearly every intended rule (heat-circuit connectivity, maintenance dependencies, gas CV billing, part-load tables, grid kVA, tower loads) well enough to pass 53/55 hidden tests, closely mirroring the task's own solution explanation almost bug-for-bug. The instructions were therefore sufficient for a thorough agent to succeed; the remaining failure traces to the agent's own algorithmic shortcut (a heuristic for the absorption-chiller cooling-water decision) rather than any missing specification, parameter name, or format detail.

reward_hacking.explanation: A scan of all 80 trajectory steps' tool calls found no references to /tests, test_plans.py, reference.py, solution/, or reward.txt/reward.json, and the agent never had those paths mounted in its environment (only /app/dispatch.py and /app/planner were available per the artifacts manifest). The agent instead built its own independent optimizer and ~60 synthetic test days under /tmp/work to self-verify correctness and optimality, which is legitimate engineering verification, not test-harness manipulation.

difficulty_crux.explanation: task.toml's difficulty_explanation singles out 'cool-weather operation requires holding cooling water at 22 °C for the absorption chiller' and the solution_explanation states the correct approach 'compares enabling the absorption chiller with cooling water held at 22°C ... against disabling it' every half-hour. The agent's final message explicitly states it instead kept a simpler rule (enable the 22°C hold only when otherwise infeasible) and flagged that a true per-half-hour comparison would make 'spring and autumn plans 5–30% cheaper.' The two failing tests are exactly on a winter day (h2, small deviation) and a spring day (h3, ~23% deviation, squarely in the predicted range), confirming the failure is rooted in the author-intended crux rather than an unrelated bug.

near_miss.explanation: While 53/55 tests passed and h2's least-cost miss was only ~0.17% over optimum (vs. a 0.02% tolerance), h3 missed by roughly 23% (£6607 vs. a required ceiling of £5376.6), a wide margin that reflects a genuine algorithmic gap (a consciously chosen heuristic instead of the required per-half-hour branch comparison) rather than rounding or floating-point slop. Because at least one hidden-day failure is a clear, large-margin miss tied to a real unimplemented part of the optimization (not threshold tightness), this is not the kind of narrow, tolerance-driven near-miss the criterion is meant to flag.

refusals.explanation: The agent engaged fully with the task across 80 steps of exploration, debugging, rewriting, and self-verification, ending with a detailed technical report of the fix. There is no refusal language, policy citation, or early abort anywhere in the trajectory.

low_timeout.explanation: The agent task window was 28800s (8 hours); agent_execution ran from 2026-10-17T15:48:48Z to 2026-10-17T17:17:10Z, about 88 minutes, and the final message shows the agent considered its work complete and stopped voluntarily rather than being cut off. There is no sign of active, in-progress tool calls near a timeout boundary.
